newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai phone firms stride on, finance turmoil aside.
newsitem.headline: Thai phone firms stride on, finance turmoil aside.

text.p: Thai fixed-line telephone companies, which reported poor results in 1996, are expected to see some turnaround this year despite turmoil in the domestic finance sector, analysts said on Wednesday.
Their fortunes could improve as they have more scope to install extra lines this year, analysts told Reuters.

"For fixed land lines, there is going to be some improvement (in 1997) because more lines will be connected. There should be some turnaround," Paul Ngo, an investment analyst at ING Baring, told Reuters.

However, Thailand's lingering economic problems, slower growth, spending cuts of more than 100 billion baht ($3.85 billion) this fiscal year and shaky financial markets could impact some firms negatively, analysts said.
TelecomAsia Plc and Thai Telephone and Telecommunication Plc are the only private operators of fixed-line telephones in Thailand.

"There might be some impact (from slower economic growth). But the existing demand and long waiting lists (for new lines) will partly help acceleration of both companies' line connections," said an analyst at Nava Finance and Securities.

TelecomAsia has a government's concession to install and operate 2.6 million telephone lines in Bangkok and nearby provinces. Thai Telephone and Telecommunication won a concession to install 1.5 million lines in the provinces.
TelecomAsia posted a loss of 1.92 billion baht in 1996 compared with profit of 1.29 billion in the previous year.
Thai Telephone's net profit in 1996 dropped 49 percent to 424.22 million baht from 830 million a year ago.
Analysts said operating expenses of the two companies rose substantially last year as they accelerated telephone line installations to meet a government deadline set for last September.
"In the case of TelecomAsia and TT&T, their revenue did not rise to offset their cost," said Keith Neruda, an analyst at Capital Nomura Securities.
TelecomAsia said in January the company had only connected 1.1 million of the 2.6 million lines that had been installed.
Thai Telephone had about 990,000 telephone lines connected to subscribers from the 1.5 million lines installed.
Hong Kong-based Seamico Marlin Securities said in a new report that TelecomAsia's revenue was expected to grow rapidly on higher revenue per telephone line.
"With the completion of the line buildout project, amortization growth is expected to level off significantly," Seamico Marlin said.

Ngo at ING Baring said most other telecom companies would continue to see a tough year in 1997 as intensifying competition and declining mobile phone handset prices will take a toll on their earnings.

Thailand's two major telecommunication conglomerates with mobile phone concessions, Shinawatra Computer and Communication Plc and United Communication Industry Plc, reported sharp drops in profit last year.

Shinawatra Computer posted a 1996 net profit of 2.63 billion baht against 3.3 billion in the previous year. United Communication's profit in 1996 was 2.4 billion baht compared with 2.8 billion in 1995.
(US$1 = 26 baht)
